title: Relative tensor product of module objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative ring object of $\mathsf{Sh}(X_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$. For $\mathcal R$-modules $M,N$, the relative tensor product $M\otimes_{\mathcal R}N$ is the coequalizer, in $\mathsf{Sh}(X_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$, of the two maps

$$
M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}N\rightrightarrows M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}N,
$$

given by the action on $M$ (after the symmetry $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal R\cong\mathcal R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}M$) and by the action on $N$. Its $\mathcal R$-action is induced by the action on $N$; because $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ preserves coequalizers in each variable (each $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}-$ is a left adjoint, governing reference, §2), this induced map is defined, and by commutativity of $\mathcal R$ it agrees with the action induced by $M$.

lean.note: Specialize the recorded def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor construction to C = Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}, R = mathcalR.X for any mathcalR : CommMon C, and M N : Mod C R. The coefficient tensor is AddCommGrpCat.monoidalCategory (tensor over the integers), and the sheaf tensor is Sheaf.monoidalCategory, the same canonical sheafification tensor used by sfbSheafTensorStructure. tensorObj_X displays exactly the two balancing arrows, tensorObjπ is their projection, and isColimitTensorπ supplies the universal property. The stored left action is induced by M (whiskerLeft_tensorπ_smul); the associated bimodule right action is induced by N (Mathlib Bimod.TensorBimod.π_tensor_id_actRight and Mod.toBimodObj_actRight). isSymmetric_tensor identifies that right action with braiding followed by the stored left action. Since the ambient category is symmetric, transporting this equality by the inverse braiding says exactly that the left action is induced by N as well. Tensor preservation of coequalizers follows from the recorded closed sheaf tensor, so no flatness or extra size equality is assumed. The complete specialization was checked by scompile.py in scratchpad/RelativeTensorSpecialization.lean. No new module or duplicate definition is introduced.
